review: Reviewed the normalized map/settings/configuration deltas and four focused suites. Website Maps keys use profile-specific browser slots; legacy origin-wide keys are not silently enrolled into an account. Native reads fail closed and explicit native records take precedence over a bundled public browser key.

Ordinary accounts retain their Maps browser-key entry. Routes credential controls retain the documented developer exception because their service credential is process-wide, not isolated to an owner. Settings describe configuration readiness separately from live API access, billing and Earth Engine registration.

Reproduced nine lifecycle failures: browser writes after account changes, native read/save/clear receipt reuse, password retention during save, old-account map notifications, loss of a new Routes draft and missing reinspection for another equally capable account.

The helper now checks initiating profile identity and revision after asynchronous boundaries, permitting initial unknown-session discovery but rejecting subsequent changes and A-to-B-to-A round trips. Retired operations do not mutate browser storage or return old native key receipts.

Settings use separate guarded mutation slots, immediate submitted-password clearing, current Routes policy checks, refreshed account-view reads and scoped provider/Routes responses. Old completions cannot clear new drafts, publish map-change events or finish a newer operation.

The map view already sequences key loads and now reloads on an account-profile change. Its delta also corrects account-sign-in recovery wording. SDK/reload behavior is reviewed source only here, not exercised against real Google Maps.

Seventeen browser checks pass: eleven lifecycle/success cases plus six prior storage/settings cases. Google-key-shaped values are deterministic short digit fixtures, never credentials. No keys from the owner, native writes, Google requests, paid inference or game operation were used.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source proposal; runtime fix 30 is not installed. Tests mock native bridge and HTTP behavior.

An already-dispatched native write may complete in its original context. Client retirement suppresses stale attribution; it is not native cancellation or rollback. Native account validation remains authoritative.
Actual SDK loading, reload timing, provider restrictions/billing, native protected storage and ordinary installed-account acceptance remain separate.

Unchanged map geometry, boundary datasets, diplomacy overlay, provider-status shapes and source interpretation are not requalified by credential tests. Diplomacy overlay additions remain a separate source cohort.
Malformed provider payloads, all same-account read/write interleavings, storage denial and all browser lifecycle variants remain separate qualifications.
No scientific operator, adapter grant, proof or certificate change. Five intentional support-contact matches remain in owner publication review.
